name: EXPO-FT
summary: Imitation-pretrained VLAs plateau at whatever their demonstrations contain, and the standard remedy — reinforcement learning finetuning — normally costs more robot interaction than anyone has. EXPO-FT targets that sample budget directly, adapting sample-efficient RL machinery to finetuning large vision-language-action policies rather than small task-specific ones. It comes out of Stanford IRIS with Dorsa Sadigh and Chelsea Finn, and lands in the same problem area as Physical Intelligence's RL-token work, which arrived a month earlier from the opposite direction.
innovation: Treats the sample budget, rather than the RL objective, as the binding constraint for VLA post-training.
matters: Two independent groups converging on cheap online RL over a frozen-ish VLA within a month suggests this is the field's current consensus next step after imitation.
limits: Summarized here from the paper listing rather than a full read; method details and results are not verified. Confirm before citing.
lineage: Sample-efficient off-policy RL in the RLPD and HIL-SERL tradition, retargeted at VLA-scale policies.
